alerts.channels_config: Channels are set in .env — email (SMTP), ntfy, Telegram, webhook, Apprise. Restart to apply changes.
alerts.channels_none: No channels configured — nothing will be sent
alerts.channels_recommended: Best pairing: ntfy for the fastest phone push — install the app, subscribe to your topic — plus email as a written record.
alerts.how_intrusion: Intrusion signals — a door, window, trunk, or frunk opening, an unlock, or the vehicle moving with no one inside — come straight from vehicle state changes, so they're reliable.
alerts.how_polled: Standard Sentry Mode triggers (someone approaches, the vehicle starts recording) are detected from center_display_state=7 — that value means Sentry Mode has been triggered and the touchscreen is showing the recording warning, not that Sentry Mode is simply on. No setup needed, but while parked your vehicle is polled every 30 seconds, so short events can be missed. For real-time detection with no gaps, connect Fleet Telemetry (see the docs).
alerts.how_sessions: Back-to-back activity merges into one session ({dedup}-second window). Anything lasting more than {escalate} seconds, or a second trigger soon after, escalates to high priority — so one busy night doesn't bury you in alerts.
alerts.no_sentry: No Sentry Mode activity yet. Once the vehicle is parked with Sentry Mode on, anyone who approaches shows up here.
alerts.policies_help: People walk past your own driveway all day — no need to hear about every one. Locations come from your saved places in Settings.
alerts.policies_intrusion_note: Intrusion alerts — door opened, vehicle unlocked — ignore this setting and are always sent.
alerts.polled_off: Polled detection is off in .env (SENTRY_POLLED_ALERTS=false). Only Fleet Telemetry and intrusion signals will alert.
alerts.test_failed: Not sent. Check the channel settings in .env
alerts.title: Sentry Mode & alerts
banner.stale: Data collection stopped {n} min ago — Sentry Mode and door alerts are not being sent. Check that everything is running:
body.idle_fee: Unplug soon — Superchargers charge by the minute once charging finishes.
cmd.error.asleep: Vehicle asleep or offline (408). Run Wake vehicle, then retry.
cmd.error.missing_param: This command needs a value for “{param}”.
cmd.error.no_eid: No Tesla vehicle ID (eid) on record for this vehicle.
cmd.error.no_location: Window control needs the vehicle's current location, and none is on record yet. Drive or wake the vehicle, then retry.
cmd.error.no_token: No Tesla API token. Connect your Tesla on the setup page, or paste an access token in Settings.
cmd.error.no_vin: No VIN on record for this vehicle. The Fleet API and the signing proxy address vehicles by VIN.
cmd.error.token_expired: Token expired (401). It refreshes on its own — retry in a minute.
cmd.error.unsigned: This vehicle requires signed commands. Deploy Tesla's vehicle-command proxy and set TESLA_COMMAND_PROXY. See docs/COMMANDS.md
cmdk.a_no_data: No data yet. This fills in once your vehicle reports.

cmdk.needs_value: Type a number first — e.g. “80” for 80{unit}.
cmdk.title: Ask your Tesla
control.confirm: Run {name}? This can leave the vehicle unlocked or unmonitored.
control.not_ready.db_down: Can't reach the database. On first start it takes a minute to initialize — refresh and retry.
control.not_ready.no_token: No Tesla API token found. Connect your Tesla on the setup page, or paste a token below.
control.not_ready.title: Commands unavailable
control.signed_note: Vehicles built after 2021 need signed commands over the Fleet API: deploy Tesla's vehicle-command proxy and set TESLA_COMMAND_PROXY. Without it, commands fail with a clear error rather than silently. If the vehicle is asleep, run Wake vehicle first.
control.title: Vehicle controls
control.token_hint: You normally don't need this. Connecting your Tesla once on the setup page is enough — the token is stored encrypted and reused for every command. Paste one here only to override it.
dashcam.empty.encryption: If clips import but won't play, check Controls → Safety → Dashcam Encryption on the touchscreen — encrypted recordings can't be read by anything other than the car.
dashcam.empty.setup: Prefer to copy files instead? Put the TeslaCam folder from the drive into data/teslacam/ on this machine, then rescan.
dashcam.empty.title: No clips yet — that's expected until you bring some in.
dashcam.empty.usb_cta: Open clips from a USB drive →
dashcam.empty.usb_why: Tesla never uploads dashcam footage anywhere — it only ever lives on the USB drive in your vehicle. Plug that drive into this computer and the USB page reads it in place: clips play and telemetry decodes in your browser, with nothing copied or uploaded. Import only the events you want to keep.
dashcam.hevc_note: {n} clips use HEVC — they'll be transcoded for playback, which takes a moment the first time.
dashcam.locked_body: The files are there and the timeline is right, but nothing can be read out of them — this is what encrypted footage looks like. Tesla can encrypt dashcam and Sentry Mode recordings on the drive; turn it off on the touchscreen under Controls → Safety → Dashcam Encryption, then record again. Clips saved while it was on stay unreadable. A partial copy off the drive looks the same way, so it's worth re-copying first.
dashcam.sei.none: No SEI data — older software, parked clip, or encrypted
dashcam.sei.title: Segment SEI stats
dashcam.status.awaiting: Folder is set up and empty — nothing imported yet
dashcam.title: Dashcam
drives.pick_hint: Select a drive to see its route
drives.track_none: No GPS data for this drive
energy.baseline_note: Leave blank to use the best range ever observed. If you installed OhmyTesla years after buying the car, that best-ever figure already includes the degradation — enter the original EPA/WLTP range to measure it properly.
energy.eff_sub: What cold weather actually costs you
energy.no_history_sub: Charging sessions and drives appear here as they happen. Data starts from the day you connected your account — Tesla's API doesn't provide history.
energy.no_rates: Rates not set — costs can't be calculated
energy.range_efficiency_sub: distance driven vs rated range used
energy.soc_exposure: Time spent at each charge level
energy.soc_note: {pct}% of parked time above 80%. Sitting at a high charge level is a known cause of calendar ageing — charge to 100% before long trips, not overnight every night.
energy.soc_note_lfp: This is an LFP pack — Tesla recommends charging it to 100% regularly, so high charge levels are not a concern here.
energy.use_sub: Added at the plug, by month
energy.vampire_note: Measured between consecutive drives with no charging in between. Sentry Mode is the usual cause — it draws 150–300 W continuously.
insights.chart.range_sub: Monthly rated range scaled to a full charge — the clearest read on capacity loss
insights.chart.temp_sub: What cold weather actually costs you
insights.tariff_hint: Set your electricity rates in Settings to see charging costs. Time-of-use plans supported.

overview.no_cars: No vehicle data yet. Connect your Tesla account and your vehicles will appear here.
overview.no_events: No clips yet. Copy your TeslaCam folder into the data folder to see them here.

player.export.title: Export video
player.hevc_tip: Clip won't play? Newer software records in HEVC, which Chrome needs hardware decoding for. Try Safari or Edge, or use Export below to make an H.264 copy. If the clip is encrypted (default on 2026.20 and later), turn off Safety → Dashcam Encryption on the touchscreen and record it again.

player.meta.title: Clip details

security.clear_confirm: Delete every alert in the history? Sentry Mode activity and the alerts themselves are unaffected.
security.email_missing_password: SMTP_HOST is set but SMTP_PASS is empty, so nothing can be sent. Gmail needs an App Password (not your login password) — generate one at myaccount.google.com/apppasswords, put it in .env, then run ./omt restart.
security.email_missing_to: SMTP_HOST is set but SMTP_TO is empty — there is nobody to send to.
security.email_missing_user: SMTP_HOST is set but SMTP_USER is empty. Fill in the account that sends the mail, then run ./omt restart.
security.no_channels_body: Sentry Mode is being watched, but no notification channel is set up — nothing will reach you. Add one and this vanishes.
security.snoozed: Muted for {n} more min — intrusion alerts still get through.
security.snoozed_all: Everything muted for {n} more min, including intrusion alerts.
sentry.notify.escalated: ⚠️ Sentry still active — someone is by your vehicle
sentry.notify.panic: 🚨 Sentry alarm — your vehicle was broken into
sentry.notify.triggered: 👀 Sentry triggered — someone is near your vehicle
sentry.policy.escalated: Only when it repeats or persists

settings.about.heading: About
settings.about.line1: OhmyTesla — a self-hosted Tesla companion built on TeslaMate. AGPL-3.0.
settings.about.line2: Not affiliated with the TeslaMate project or Tesla, Inc.
settings.about.line3: Everything else — notification channels, TeslaCam folder, portal password, map tiles — lives in .env at the project root. Run docker compose up -d after editing.
settings.abrp_off: ABRP relay is off. Set ABRP_ENABLED and ABRP_TOKEN in .env to feed your real data to A Better Routeplanner.
settings.bridge.enable_ok: SentryMode streaming on for {configured} vehicles. Takes effect the next time each one connects.
settings.bridge.heading: Live Sentry Mode stream (hosted relay)
settings.bridge.help_experimental: This relay's protocol hasn't been verified against a live account. If no events arrive, adjust the FLEET_BRIDGE_* settings against docs/FLEET-TELEMETRY.md.
settings.bridge.help_verified: Leave SENTRY_POLLED_ALERTS=true: polling stands down while the stream is live and takes back over if the relay fails or runs out of quota.
settings.bridge.intro: Out of the box, Sentry Mode alerts are inferred from polling, so brief events slip past. A hosted telemetry relay gives you Tesla's live state stream instead — Aware means someone is close, Panic means the alarm fired — within seconds and with nothing dropped. No public IP required: the hub opens the connection outbound.
settings.bridge.no_events: Connected, but no events have arrived. The relay most likely isn't sending the SentryMode field yet — use the button below.
settings.bridge.no_vehicles: Not connected yet — no VIN on record. Connect your Tesla account and it syncs automatically.
settings.bridge.off_help:
To enable, set these in .env at the project root:
FLEET_BRIDGE_ENABLED=true
FLEET_BRIDGE_PROVIDER=teslemetry
FLEET_BRIDGE_TOKEN=your-token
then run docker compose up -d. See the fleet-telemetry docs and docs/FLEET-TELEMETRY.md.
settings.car_saved_restart: Saved. Run ./omt restart for it to take effect — TeslaMate caches these until it restarts.
settings.channels_note: Email, ntfy, Telegram, webhook and Apprise are configured in .env — restart to apply.
settings.data_export_help: Everything, in formats other tools can read. Nothing here is locked to OhmyTesla.
settings.data_ok_long: No gaps or missing records found in the last 90 days.
settings.detect_none: No region signals found. Connect your Tesla account for a better guess.
settings.env_note: Notification channels, the dashcam folder, the portal password and map tiles live in .env. Run ./omt restart after editing.
settings.ice_help: Enter what a comparable petrol car would use and what fuel costs you. Leave blank and the comparison stays hidden rather than guessing on your behalf.
settings.issue_charges_without_cost: {n} charging session(s) have no cost. Set your rates and press Recompute.
settings.issue_drives_without_track: {n} drive(s) have no GPS track, so their map will be empty.
settings.issue_gaps: {n} gap(s) with no data at all — the collector was probably down.
settings.issue_missing_addresses: {n} trip endpoint(s) have no address — reverse geocoding failed or timed out.
settings.maint_help: Tesla has no fixed service schedule, but tyre rotation, filters and brake fluid still run on distance or time. Mark an item done and the clock restarts from today.
settings.mcp_hint: Ask an AI assistant about your car: claude mcp add --transport http ohmytesla http://localhost:8800/mcp
settings.places_confirm: Remove this place? Past drives and charges keep their history.
settings.places_note: Name the places you park often. Charging costs, Sentry Mode policies and drive endpoints all use these names instead of raw addresses.
settings.push.heading: Notifications
settings.push.insecure_origin:
Browsers disable Web Push on insecure origins, and this page is served from {origin}.
Reach it at http://localhost:8800 instead, or put the portal behind an HTTPS reverse proxy — Tailscale and similar give you a trusted certificate. ntfy, Telegram, and email alerts are unaffected.
settings.push.intro: Native browser push, no third-party account. On iPhone, add this page to your Home Screen first, then turn push on — a Safari requirement, iOS 16.4 and later. Android and desktop Chrome work as is.
settings.push.need_permission: Push needs notification permission. If no prompt appeared, check notification settings for this site in your browser.
settings.push.unsupported: This browser doesn't support Web Push. On iPhone, add this page to your Home Screen and open it from there.
settings.sleep_note: Sleep settings control how long the logger waits before letting the vehicle sleep. Longer waits capture more detail; shorter waits reduce standby drain.
settings.speed_limit: Speed alert when nobody is in the car
settings.speed_limit_help: Useful when someone else has the car. Leave blank to turn it off.
settings.sub: Everything here is optional. The defaults work.
settings.tariff.default_heading: Default rate (AC charging and unlisted locations)
settings.tariff.dirty: ℹ Rates changed. Run Recompute to update past charges.
settings.tariff.heading: Electricity rates (automatic charging costs)
settings.tariff.intro: Set your electricity rates once and every charging session is priced automatically — time-of-use plans included, split across rate periods by the clock. No typing a cost in by hand.
settings.tariff.loc_note: Locations come from your saved places. Home is often on a time-of-use plan; charging at work may be free.
settings.tariff.saved: Saved. Run Recompute to apply it to past charges.
settings.tariff.template_applied: Template applied — now enter your rates and save.
settings.tariff.template_note: fills the time bands only — you enter the rates
settings.tariff.unconfigured: Rates are still all zero. Set them first — nothing was written back.
settings.tariff.uncovered: · {uncovered_sessions} sessions ran outside your rate periods
settings.tariff.warn_bad_period: {scope}: period “{period}” has an invalid start or end time.
settings.tariff.warn_gap: {scope}: {hours}h {minutes}m isn’t covered by any period — energy used then is billed as 0.
settings.tariff.writeback_off: Set COST_WRITE_BACK=true in .env to save costs to the database, so Grafana shows them too.
settings.tariff.writeback_on: Write-back is on: costs are saved to the database and show up in Grafana.
settings.title: Settings
settings.token.heading: Tesla API token (for vehicle commands)
settings.token.placeholder: Leave empty to use the token from sign-in
settings.units_note: Language and units are separate: Canada reads English but measures in km and °C, the UK drives in miles but reads °C. Switching language changes only the defaults — anything you set by hand stays put.
setup.db_waiting: Waiting for the database to finish setting up…
setup.lede: One-time setup. After this, everything runs on its own.
setup.privacy: Tokens are stored encrypted on this machine and never leave it except to talk to Tesla.
setup.step1_note: Tesla no longer lets third-party apps sign in with an email and password. A small helper opens Tesla's own login page and hands back two tokens. Your password only ever goes to Tesla.
setup.title: Connect your Tesla
setup.waiting_vehicle: Connected. Waiting for your vehicle to report in — a minute or two, or until it wakes up.

token.src_env: Using the token from the environment
trips.pick_hint: Select a trip to see its route
usb.drop.hint: Plug the USB drive into this computer, then pick the TeslaCam folder — or the whole drive. You can also drag the folder in.
usb.drop.privacy: Nothing is uploaded. Clips play and SEI telemetry decodes in your browser. Only the clips you import go to the server, for exports and data overlays.
usb.empty: No TeslaCam clips found. Pick the root of the USB drive or the TeslaCam folder.
usb.hevc: Won't play? HEVC needs hardware decoding in the browser — try Safari or Edge. Or import the clip and export it as H.264.
usb.import.desc: Once imported you can export an MP4, overlay battery, power, and elevation data, and keep the clip archived.
